questions.question: The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress was ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Lala Lajpat Rai__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

All India Trade Union Congress:

__
 
• The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) is the oldest trade union federation in India.
 
• It is associated with the Communist Party of India.
 
• According to provisional statistics from the Ministry of Labour, AITUC had a membership of 14.2 million in 2013.
 
• It was founded on 31 October 1920 with Lala Lajpat Rai as its first president.
 
• Until 1945 when unions became organised on party lines, it was the primary trade union organisation in India.
 
• The main purpose of labour unions is to give workers the power to negotiate for more favourable working conditions and other benefits through collective bargaining.
 
• The following are the objectives of a trade union:
 
 
• To improve the economic lot of workers by securing them better wages.
 
• To secure workers better working conditions.
 
• To secure bonuses for the workers from the profits of the enterprise/organization.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **C Rajagopalachari**

 
 
• C. Rajagopalachari (1878-1972) was an Indian lawyer, writer and independence activist.
 
• He was popular as **Rajaji, C.R. and Mootharignar Rajaji.**
 
• He was the **last Governor-General **before India became a republic.
 
• He is remembered for his contribution to the independence struggle as well as his intellectual and administrative prowess.
 
• **In 1954, he was honoured with India’s highest civilian award, Bharat Ratna.**
 
 
 
• **Chandra Shekhar Azad**
 
 
• ​Azad was born on 23rd July 1906 in the Alirajpur district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Chandra Shekhar, then a 15-year-old student, joined a Non-Cooperation Movement in December 1921. As a result, he was arrested.
 
• On being presented before a magistrate, he gave his name as "Azad" (The Free), his father's name as "Swatantrata" (Independence) and his residence as "Jail". Therefore, he came to be known as Chandra Shekhar Azad.
 
• After the suspension of the non-cooperation movement in 1922 by Gandhi, Azad joined Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
 
• Most of the fund collection for revolutionary activities was done through robberies of government property. In line with the same, Kakori Train Robbery near Kakori, Lucknow was done in 1925 by HRA.
 
• He died at Azad Park in Allahabad on 27th February 1931.
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru**
 
 
• **​**Pandit Motilal Nehru was a lawyer and politician who was born in the year 1861.
 
• He was elected to United Provinces Council__ in 1909.
 
• He was contemporary of Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.
 
• He attended the **Delhi Durbar in 1911 **in honour of the visit of King George V.
 
• Motilal was elected **President of the United Province Congress in the year 1911**.

questions.question: The Anushilan Samiti was active in which part of the Indian subcontinent in the 20th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Anushilan Samiti:

 
 
• **The Anushilan Samiti** was founded by Pramathanath Mitra and includes Jatindranath Banerjee, Barindra Kumar Ghosh and others.
 
• In April 1906, an inner circle within Anushilan (Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Bhupendranath Dutta) started the weekly Yugantar and conducted a few abortive ‘actions’.
 
• In 1907, an abortive attempt was made by the Yugantar group on the life of a very unpopular British official, Sir Fuller
 
• Anushilan group was arrested including the Ghosh brothers, Aurobindo and Barindra, who were tried in the Alipore conspiracy case, variously called Manicktolla bomb conspiracy or Muraripukur conspiracy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pramathanath Mitra founded the Anushilan Samiti on March 24, 1902.
 
• It had two branches:
 
 
• the Jugantar Group in Calcutta
 
• the Dhaka Anushilan Samiti in Dhaka.
 
 
 
• The Samiti published "Bhavani Mandir" in 1905.
 
• They advocated military training in their 1907 publication, "Vartaman Rananiti."
 
• As a division of Anushilan Samiti, Dhaka Anushilan Samiti was established in November 1905. Pulin Bihar Das served as its leader when it was established.
 
• After Pulin Das was detained in the Barisal Conspiracy case in 1913, the development of this samiti was put on hold.
 
• Additionally, it should be noted that Dhaka Anushilan Samiti did not take part in the German World War I plot.
 
• Anushilan Samiti was an Indian health club that anti-British revolutionaries utilised as a covert organisation.
 
• In the early half of the 20th century, it encouraged the use of revolutionary violence to overthrow the British in India.
 
• In Bengal, in 1902, a combination of neighbourhood gyms and youth organisations came together to form the organisation.
 
• It had two significant, albeit independent, branches in East and West Bengal: the Jugantar group and Dhaka Anushilan Samiti, which was based in Dhaka (centred in Calcutta).

questions.question: The claim for ‘swarajya’ or self-government within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in 1906 by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The claim for **"swarajya" or self-government** within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in the **Calcutta session of 1906.**
 
• The session was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, who is considered the **"Grand Old Man of India" **for his contributions to the Indian independence movement. 
 
• In his presidential address, Naoroji called for **"self-government or swaraj like the United Kingdom or the colonies"** of Australia or Canada. 
 
• This was a significant shift in the Congress's position, as it had previously been more focused on seeking limited reforms within the British Raj.
 
• The Calcutta session's resolution on swaraj was a compromise between the **"moderates" and "extremists"** within the Congress. 
 
• The **moderates, led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, wanted to pursue a gradual path to self-government, while the extremists, led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, wanted to demand complete independence. 
 
• The resolution on swaraj represented a middle ground, calling for self-government within the British Empire, but with a degree of autonomy that would be similar to that of self-governing colonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:**

 
 
• He was an** Indian author, politician, and freedom warrior.**
 
• He was commonly referred to as **Punjab Kesari.**
 
• He was one of the **Lal Bal Pal trimurti's three members. **
 
 
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal:**
 
 
• He was a member of the** trio known as "Lal Bal Pal."**
 
• Along with** Sri Aurobindo**, Pal was one of the primary designers of the **Swadeshi movement.**

questions.question: Which of the following was a system of indigo cultivation in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nij**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nij** was a system of indigo cultivation in British India.
 
• There were two main systems of indigo cultivation – **nij and ryoti.**
 
• Within the system of** nij cultivation**, the planter produced indigo in lands that he directly controlled.
 
• He either bought the land or rented it from other **zamindars and produced indigo by directly employing hired labourers.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Indigo **could be cultivated on bonded land**, which were already densely populated. 
 
• Only small plots scattered over the landscape could be acquired. 
 
• Planters needed large areas in compact blocks to cultivating indigo in plantations.
 
• They attempted to lease in the land around the indigo factory, and evict the peasants from the area. 
 
• 
 
Those living around the indigo factory faced eviction from their land and it always led to conflicts and tension.

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji **offered a scathing criticism of the economic impact of British rule in India through his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

 
• Dadabhai Naoroji, the “Grand Old Man of India”, was the the first Indian member of the British parliament.
 
• In 1865 and 1866, Naoroji helped found the London Indian Society and the East India Association respectively.
 
• He was Congress president thrice, in 1886, 1893, and 1906.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Surendranath supported Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms, unlike Congress, and with many liberal leaders he left Congress and founded a new organization named Indian National Liberation Federation in 1919.
 
 
 
• Badruddin Tyabji was an Indian political activist during British Raj.
 
 
• He was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He served as the third President of the Indian National Congress from 1887 to 1888.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters was accused of killing Michael o Dwyer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Udham Singh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
Udham Singh, a prominent figure in the Indian independence movement, was accused of killing Sir Michael O'Dwyer, a former Lieutenant Governor of the Punjab province during British rule in India. The incident took place in the aftermath of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, a tragic event where British troops under General Reginald Dyer opened fire on a peaceful gathering in Amritsar on April 13, 1919.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre: **
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre was a turning point in India's struggle for independence, leading to widespread outrage and condemnation.
 
• General Dyer's brutal action resulted in the death of hundreds of innocent Indians and left a lasting impact on the collective psyche of the nation.
 
• **Udham Singh's Motivation: **
 
• Udham Singh was deeply affected by the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, witnessing the brutality firsthand as a teenager.
 
• He pledged to avenge the atrocity and sought justice for the victims, particularly holding responsible those in positions of authority.
 
• **Assassination of Michael O'Dwyer:** 
 
• On March 13, 1940, Udham Singh carried out the assassination of Sir Michael O'Dwyer in London during a meeting of the East India Association.
 
• O'Dwyer, who had endorsed Dyer's actions in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, was seen by Singh as a symbol of British oppression in India.
 
• **Trial and Execution:** 
 
• Udham Singh was arrested immediately after the assassination and put on trial.
 
• During the trial, he declared that he had acted to avenge the victims of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• Udham Singh was convicted of murder and subsequently executed on July 31, 1940. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Udham Singh's actions were seen by many as a courageous act of resistance against colonial oppression, and he became a symbol of the struggle for Indian independence.
 
• The British government's response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the subsequent events contributed to the intensification of the independence movement in India.
 
• Udham Singh's legacy is remembered in India for his sacrifice and determination in seeking justice for the victims of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• In summary, Udham Singh, motivated by the horrific events of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, took the drastic step of assassinating Michael O'Dwyer as a form of retribution and justice for the victims. His actions reflect the deep impact of historical atrocities on individuals and the role of such events in shaping the course of the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: _______, a lawyer from East Bengal, was especially active in the Non-Cooperation movement.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittaranjan Das.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chittaranjan Das** a lawyer from East Bengal, was especially active in the Non-Cooperation movement.

 
• Chittaranjan Das is popularly known as 'Deshbandhu'.
 
• He is the first president of the Swaraj Party (1923). 
 
• C.R. Das served as the Indian National Congress president in the Ahmedabad session (1921).
 
• He was actively involved in Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He became involved with the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• In 1908, Das attained widespread fame when he was successfully able to defend Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak raised the slogan, “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!”.

 
 
• The word Swarajya was first coined by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was also known as Lokmanya Tilak.
 
• He established a prominent organization Deccan Education Society to promote modern learning.
 
• He also established Fergusson College at Pune.
 
• He along with Annie Besant played an important role during Home Rule Movement(1916-18).
 
• Kesari and Mahratta were the two newspapers started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
 
 
 
• ​Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel popularly known as Sardar Patel was an Indian statesman.
 
 
• He served as the First Deputy Prime Minister of India.
 
• He was an Indian barrister and a senior leader of the Indian National Congress who played a leading role in the country's struggle for independence and guided its integration into a united, independent nation. 
 
• His commitment to national integration in the newly independent country was total and uncompromising, earning him the sobriquet "Iron Man of India".
 
 
 
• **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar **came from an untouchable caste called the Mahars.
 
 
• Through modern methods, he integrated untouchables into Indian society.
 
• He established the Samaj Samta Sangh in 1927 to propagate the gospel of social equality between untouchables and Hindu castes.
 
• Additionally, he organized temple entry movements.
 
• Ambedkar emerged as one of the major leaders of the depressed classes before the Round Table Conference in 1930-31.
 
• He demanded constitutional safeguards for the depressed classes.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Satyagraha Ashram founded by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1915.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Satyagraha Ashram at Ahmedabad is the place where Mahatma Gandhi lived after he returned from South Africa in 1915.
 
• The “Satyagraha Ashrama” was founded by Mahatama Gandhi at Kocharab__ near Ahmedabad in the year 1915.
 
• Later in 1917, the ashram was shifted to Sabarmati and came to be known as the “Sabarmati Ashram”.
 
• The ashram was relocated because Gandhiji wanted to carry out agricultural activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Mahatma Gandhi is known as the Father of the Nation and is commonly called Bapu.
 
• His birthday on 2 October is commemorated in India as Gandhi Jayanti, a national holiday.
 
• He was a prolific writer. One of Gandhi's publications Hind Swaraj was published in Gujarati in 1909.
 
• He was the leader of various movements (Satyagraha, Champaran Movement, Kheda Movement).
 
• On 9th January, we celebrate Pravasi Bharatiya Divas or NRI Day because Gandhiji returned to India on this day from South Africa in 1915. 
 
• He became the president of Congress during its Belgaum session, 1924.

questions.question: Which Indian personality was given knighthood by the British monarch but it was returned by him after the Jallianwala massacre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Rabindranath Tagore.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore **returned knighthood after the Jallianwala massacre.
 
• The** eldest son of Debendranath Tagore** was** Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941).**
 
• In opposition to the** 1919 Amritsar Massacre, **which was so cruel that it killed at least 379 unarmed protesters in the **Jallianwala Bagh**, **Rabindranath Tagore returned **his knighthood for contributions to literature.
 
• **King George V knighted him in the 1915 Birthday** Honours, but following the **1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre, **Tagore repudiated the honour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajagopalachari was among the first people** to be awarded the **Bharat Ratna, **the highest civilian honour in India. He also created the **Swatantra Party. **
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal **was a supporter of Indian nationalism, a writer, an orator, a social reformer, and a **freedom fighter for the Indian** independence struggle. He was one of the** "Lal Bal Pal" trio's three members.**
 
• In the era of British colonial control in India,** Chittaranjan Das, also known as Deshbandhu,** was a lawyer, political activist, and liberation fighter for India. He also founded and served as the leader of the **Swaraj Party in Bengal.**

questions.question: Under whose advice did Mahatma Gandhi decide to travel throughout India for a year, getting to know the land and its people since arriving in India from South Africa in 1915?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Gopal Krishna Gokhale.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** advised Mahatma Gandhi to decide to travel throughout India for a year, getting to know the land and its people since arriving in India from South Africa in 1915.
 
• During the Indian Independence Movement, Gopal Krishna Gokhale was an Indian liberal political leader and a social reformer.
 
• He was a senior leader of the National Indian Congress and the founder of the Indian Servants Society.
 
• In the formative years of this latter, Gokhale was famously a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• Gokhale visited South Africa in 1912, at the invitation of Gandhi.
 
• As a young barrister, Gandhi came back from his struggles in South Africa against the Empire and received personal advice from Gokhale, including awareness and understanding of India and the problems facing common Indians.
 
• By 1931, as the leader of the **Indian Independence Movement, Gandhi emerged.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandit Motilal Nehru was a lawyer and politician who was born in the year 1861.**

 
 
• Motilal Nehru was elected to United Provinces Council in 1909.
 
• He was a contemporary of Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.
 
• He attended the Delhi Durbar in 1911 in honour of the visit of King George V.
 
• Motilal was elected President of the United Province Congress in the year 1911.
 
 
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak raised the slogan, “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!”.
 
 
• The word Swarajya was first coined by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was also known as Lokmanya Tilak.
 
• He established a prominent organization Deccan Education Society to promote modern learning.
 
• He also established Fergusson College in Pune.
 
 
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose
 
 
• He was affectionately called Netaji and was one of the most prominent leaders of the Indian Freedom Struggle.
 
• He acknowledged Chittaranjan Das as his political guru.
 
• He was elected President of the Haripura Congress Session in 1938.
 
• He was re-elected as the President of Congress in Tripuri Session in 1939.
 
• He formed a progressive group called Forward Block.
 
• In January 1941, Subhas Chandra Bose disappeared from his home and reached Germany.

questions.question: In which year did the British Government announce Morley - Minto Reforms in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1909**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Council Act also known as Morley Minto Reforms was introduced in 1909 by Lord Minto then viceroy of India**.
 
• The main aim of these reforms **is to pacify the Indian Political Parties, especially Congress** and the **Muslim League to mark the importance of Indian Leaders in the Governmen**t.
 
• For appeasing communities **separate electorates on the basis of religion were given in this reform.**
 
• **Muslims were given a separate electorate**, they could now have their own representative members at the Legislative Councils.
 
• The **Indians were included in the councils, where ultimate decisions were made, of the India Secretory and Viceroy**.​ ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Mayo is also known as the **father of the Communal Electorate In India**.
 
• There was a hidden motive of Britishers to deviate Muslims from the **Nationalist Movement** by granting them separate electorates under the policy of **Divide and Rule.**

 
 

 **1905**
 Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon on 16 October.
 
 

 **1932**
 

 British Prime Minister, Ramsay Macdonald announced the "Communal Award" to grant separate electorates to Indian minority communities.
 
 

 **1919**
 Montague Chelmsford reform was introduced by the British Government.
